title: Biodiversity Solutions and Tradeoffs Review Test
description: Spaced review for evaluate human-impact solutions using biodiversity data, constraints, tradeoffs, and evidence-based design reasoning.

questions.prompt: What makes a biodiversity solution evidence-based?
questions.questionText: What makes a biodiversity solution evidence-based?
options: It uses data to identify the problem and test the result.
It has a nice name only.
questions.correctAnswer: It uses data to identify the problem and test the result.
questions.explanation: Evidence is needed before and after.

options: a perfect solution with no limits
a choice where one benefit comes with a cost or limitation
questions.correctAnswer: a choice where one benefit comes with a cost or limitation

questions.prompt: Which data best tests a native garden project?
questions.questionText: Which data best tests a native garden project?
options: pollinator counts before and after planting
questions.correctAnswer: pollinator counts before and after planting

questions.prompt: A plan is cheap but damages nesting habitat. What should be considered?
questions.questionText: A plan is cheap but damages nesting habitat. What should be considered?

options: impact data -> goal -> options -> tradeoff comparison -> monitor results
questions.correctAnswer: impact data -> goal -> options -> tradeoff comparison -> monitor results

options: to prove all solutions are perfect
to see whether the solution actually works
questions.correctAnswer: to see whether the solution actually works

options: Plan C has a short title.
Plan C was first on the list.
Plan C increased native plant cover by 35% and stayed under budget.
questions.correctAnswer: Plan C increased native plant cover by 35% and stayed under budget.
questions.explanation: Strong claims use data and constraints.

options: assuming lowest cost automatically means best solution
questions.correctAnswer: assuming lowest cost automatically means best solution
questions.explanation: Cost matters but is not the only criterion.

questions.prompt: Which result suggests revision is needed?
questions.questionText: Which result suggests revision is needed?
options: target species continue declining after the solution
questions.correctAnswer: target species continue declining after the solution

questions.prompt: How can a wildlife crossing help?
questions.questionText: How can a wildlife crossing help?
options: by reconnecting habitat separated by roads
questions.correctAnswer: by reconnecting habitat separated by roads

options: Reduce invasive plant cover from 40% to 15% by spring.
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce invasive plant cover from 40% to 15% by spring.

options: A solution may help some organisms more than others.
questions.correctAnswer: A solution may help some organisms more than others.

questions.prompt: Which question transfers the design rule?
questions.questionText: Which question transfers the design rule?
options: Which option best meets the goal with evidence and acceptable tradeoffs?
Which option has the most words?
questions.correctAnswer: Which option best meets the goal with evidence and acceptable tradeoffs?
questions.explanation: This applies the design decision rule.

questions.prompt: Why is an imperfect solution sometimes useful?
questions.questionText: Why is an imperfect solution sometimes useful?
options: It can improve outcomes while managing real limits.
questions.correctAnswer: It can improve outcomes while managing real limits.

options: Best solution means evidence plus tradeoffs.
questions.correctAnswer: Best solution means evidence plus tradeoffs.
